newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's Peters seeks detailed, public deal.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's Peters seeks detailed, public deal.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Wednesday said he expected a coalition deal to be detailed and to be made public.

"We want to know exactly where we are going so everyone in the country might know where our agreement is. It will be public and there will be no suprises," Peters told reporters after the sixth round of talks with the caretaker National party government.
Asked what the agreement would include, Peters said: "Policies, personalities, implementation and how the coalition will behave amongst its partners and (the) public."
New Zealand First holds the balance of power after last month's election and is negotiating with both the caretaker National Party government and the Labour Party over coalitions.
Asked if he expected to declare a preference and cease negotiations with one of the parties, Peters said: "We are going to have to sooner or later, but we can't do that until we have the details."
He would not forecast how long negotiations with both parties would continue.
Peters said talks with National on Wednesday had gone well and good progress had been made. "They went very very well. We made a lot of progress today," he said after the two and a half hour meeting.
"The longer that coalition talks have gone internationally, the more stable and durable those coalitions have been. That is our objective this time," he said.
Peters said a subcommittee including deputy leader Tau Henare and MP Peter McCardle had been established to work on the issue of state house rent rises. A round of rent revisions is now underway.
"We think it is very urgent, but we would like to know in greater depth the subject we are dealing with here. We are trying to get it resolved over the next day or two," he said.

Earlier Prime Minister Jim Bolger said he would brief Labour leader Helen Clark on Thursday on the APEC leaders forum in Subic Bay in the Philippines in late November. Bolger has received the conditional backing of New Zealand First to attend if he is still caretaker prime minister at the time.
Bolger told journalists the negotiations with New Zealand First saw another good session of talks.
He said he would make an announcement later in the week on the reallocation of portfolios from retiring ministers.
Retiring Trade Minister Philip Burdon's portfolio is expected to be assigned to Deputy Prime Minister Don McKinnon who also holds the foreign affairs portfolio.
